**Chemical — Nerve Agents:**

Organophosphate nerve agents work by inhibiting acetylcholinesterase (AChE), the enzyme that breaks down the neurotransmitter acetylcholine at nerve synapses. When AChE is inhibited, acetylcholine accumulates, causing continuous nerve stimulation — muscle spasms, secretions, eventual respiratory failure.

The major nerve agents:
- G-series (developed by Germany, WWII era): Tabun (GA), Sarin (GB), Soman (GD)
- V-series (developed post-WWII): VX, VR
- Novichok agents (Soviet-era): A-230, A-232, A-234
